Definition: from G659; a laying aside (literally or figuratively):--putting away (off).
BiblicalUsage: The word is a laying aside. Baptism is not the putting away of the filth of the flesh but the answer of a good conscience toward God, and Peter says he must shortly put off this tabernacle of his body, as Christ had shown him.
TheologicalSignificance: Baptism lays aside the old life, and death lays aside the body, and neither is the end of the story.
